subject: Order Form: Third-party IP indemnity — scope & control
messages:
From: Elena Soto <esoto@heliohealth.com>

Cc: Mark Daniels <mdaniels@heliohealth.com>, ProcureOps <procure@heliohealth.com>
Date: 2027-03-09T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Order Form redlines — IP indemnity

Aditya — attaching our redline to the order form. Legal is asking for a broader third‑party IP indemnity that: (1) covers infringement claims arising from the service as delivered; (2) includes a rebuttable presumption that customer use within documented API limits is covered; and (3) keeps defense control with the provider only if agreed in writing.

Key asks from Helio:
- Broad indemnity for third‑party IP claims tied to Redwood’s implementation and model hosting.
- Prompt evidence and cooperation obligations but a requirement that Redwood can’t unilaterally settle without customer consent unless to limit liability.
- No explicit cap tied to fees — they want a commercial cap of $5M.

We know this will be a sticking point. Please let me know Redwood’s position and whether you can share a counter.

Attachments: HelioOrderForm_redline.pdf (PDF, 92KB)

Thanks,
Elena Soto
Head of Legal, HelioHealth

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-09T11:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Order Form redlines — IP indemnity (legal take)

Team — read Helio’s redline. High level legal position and suggested compromise for commercial:

1) Scope: Redwood can accept indemnity for third‑party claims to the extent the claim arises from: (a) Redwood’s hosted service (i.e., the runtime, infra, or model artifacts we ship) and (b) the customer’s use within the documented API and the agreed configuration (no coverage where customer materially modifies the integration or uses it outside the agreed scope).

2) Defense & settlement: Redwood requests control of defense for operational efficiency, with an advance notice + right for customer to reasonably object to a proposed settlement that would materially affect customer rights. We suggest a covenant that Redwood will not settle a claim that expressly admits customer wrongdoing or imposes obligations on the customer without prior consent.

3) Cap & insurance: We cannot accept an uncapped $5M demand for order-form customers. Proposed commercial compromise: a per‑claim cap equal to the greater of (i) 12 months of fees paid under the Order Form or (ii) $1,000,000. Additionally, Redwood will maintain commercial general liability and IP insurance and will offer an insurance‑offset clause (insurance proceeds reduce indemnity exposure).

4) Evidence & cooperation: Customer must provide prompt notice, reasonable access to evidence, and a single point of contact. We should also incorporate an evidence checklist (see attachment) to speed triage.

5) Exclusions: Exclude claims arising from (i) customer data/content (including prompts and training data the customer supplies), (ii) customer modifications, and (iii) use of the service to produce outputs that infringe (i.e., Redwood will not indemnify for customer‑generated outputs where the customer’s prompts directly caused the infringing output).

Operational note: Any exception for defense control (customer keeps control) should be narrowly negotiated and reserved for very large customers or specific statutory risk. Helio is mid‑market; we should try to keep defense control with Redwood but soften settlement language.

If you want, I’ll draft a short paragraph we can share as a redline.

—Kim

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-10T08:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Order Form redlines — IP indemnity (commercial context)

Kim / Aditya — quick commercial context:
- Helio is asking for standard language for their procurement — they’ve flagged this as gating the PO.
- Revenue at stake: $480k ARR, three-year order form at commit. Losing the cap would push pricing erosion.
- Customer sensitivity: they dislike unilateral settlement language; they want a seat at the table on material outcomes.

Recommendation: accept Kimberly’s scope/defense framework but soften the settlement carve to include a notice-and‑consult process (we control defense; if customer pays a portion of settlement or provides written consent, we can proceed). Offer upgraded evidence support (fast triage and a named escrow contact) as a commercial sweetener.

If Kimberly can draft one paragraph and a short “how we handle claims” FAQ (2 bullets) I can attach to the commercial redline — helps procurement move faster.

—Laura

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Soto <esoto@heliohealth.com>
Cc: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-12T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Order Form redlines — IP indemnity (Redwood counterproposal)

Elena — thanks again for the redline and the context. We’ve discussed internally and can propose the following counter to move the PO forward. High level summary: scope limited to Redwood‑controlled elements, Redwood control of defense with a customer consult/consent for material settlements, a per‑claim cap tied to fees or a $1M floor, and clarified exclusions for customer content/outputs.

Proposed order form paragraph (redline attached):
• Redwood will indemnify, defend and hold harmless HelioHealth from third‑party claims alleging that the licensed Redwood service as delivered by Redwood infringes or misappropriates such third party’s intellectual property, provided that: (a) HelioHealth provides prompt written notice and reasonable cooperation; (b) the claim arises from Redwood’s hosted runtime, model artifacts, or service implementation (not from HelioHealth’s data, prompts, or customer modifications); and (c) Redwood receives sole conduct of the defense, provided Redwood shall not settle a claim that expressly admits HelioHealth’s wrongdoing or imposes obligations on HelioHealth without HelioHealth’s prior written consent.

Commercial cap: per‑claim cap equal to the greater of (i) 12 months of fees paid under the Order Form and (ii) $1,000,000. Insurance offset: any recoveries from Redwood’s insurance will reduce Redwood’s indemnity obligations.

Evidence: we’ve attached an evidence_request_matrix.xlsx that lists the minimal items we’ll need to triage a claim (sample notice template, log exports, and contact for legal/tech). We’ll also provide a named Redwood claims engineer to speed evidence collection where needed.

Next steps: I’ve attached our redline and a two‑bullet FAQ we propose to include in the order form appendix. If Helio accepts in principle, we can prepare a DocuSign for signature and move to invoice.

Attachments: RedwoodCounter_redline.pdf (PDF, 48KB), evidence_request_matrix.xlsx (XLSX, 24KB)

Aditya / team — thanks for the quick turnaround and the proposed paragraph. Helio can accept the scope carveouts you’ve described and the per‑claim cap you propose, subject to two clarifications: (1) confirm the timeframe for Redwood to notify Helio and produce the evidence checklist items (we’d like 5 business days for initial notice acknowledgment and 10 business days for the initial evidence packet); and (2) confirm the settlement approval process — we need a written consent step for any settlement that would materially impair Helio’s products or data.

If you confirm those two items I’ll route to procurement for execution and we can sign the DocuSign link you provided.

Thanks,
Elena
